questions.question: Which of the following expressions correctly represents the order of magnitude for the Kelvin-Helmholtz timescale (\(\tau_{\text{KH}}\)) of a star with mass \(M\), radius \(R\), and luminosity \(L\)?
options: \(\frac{G M R}{L^2}\)
\(\frac{G M^2}{R L}\)
\(\frac{G M}{R L}\)

questions.question: Limb darkening in the optical continuum spectrum of a normal stellar atmosphere occurs primarily because an observer looking near the stellar limb:
options: sees light originating predominantly from deeper, hotter atmospheric layers compared to the disk center.
views regions dominated entirely by coherent electron scattering rather than absorption.
sees light originating predominantly from higher, cooler atmospheric layers compared to the disk center.
observes higher line-of-sight dust extinction within the circumstellar envelope.

questions.question: In general relativity, the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff (TOV) equation describes the hydrostatic equilibrium of a compact star. How do relativistic effects alter the dynamic equilibrium compared to the Newtonian regime?
options: Thermal pressure exerts a repulsive gravitational influence, reducing the required internal pressure gradient.
Gravitational time dilation reduces the effective mass of the stellar core, allowing for arbitrarily high equilibrium masses.
Frame-dragging completely cancels out the radial pressure gradient near the stellar surface.
Pressure and internal energy density act as additional sources of gravity, requiring a steeper pressure gradient to maintain equilibrium.

questions.question: In hierarchical three-body celestial mechanics, the Kozai-Lidov mechanism induces long-term, secular oscillations primarily between which two orbital parameters of the inner binary?
options: Eccentricity and inclination
Semi-major axis and eccentricity
Longitude of the ascending node and semi-major axis
Orbital period and argument of periastron

questions.question: During heavy-element stellar nucleosynthesis, the rapid neutron-capture process (r-process) differs fundamentally from the slow neutron-capture process (s-process) because in the r-process:
options: beta-decay occurs much faster than successive neutron captures.
the neutron-capture rate is much faster than the characteristic beta-decay rate of the unstable nuclei.
alpha-capture reactions completely bypass the need for free neutron flux.
high-energy neutrino spallation replaces free neutron capture entirely.
